Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the quality of the responses provided by two AI assistants to the user prompt displayed below. You will be given assistant A's answer and assistant B's answer. Your job is to evaluate which assistant's answer is better.

Begin your evaluation by generating your own answer to the prompt. You must provide your answers before judging any answers.

When evaluating the assistants' answers, compare both assistants' answers with your answer. You must identify and correct any mistakes or inaccurate information.

Then consider if the assistant's answers are helpful, relevant, and concise. Helpful means the answer correctly responds to the prompt or follows the instructions. Note when user prompt has any ambiguity or more than one interpretation, it is more helpful and appropriate to ask for clarifications or more information from the user than providing an answer based on assumptions. Relevant means all parts of the response closely connect or are appropriate to what is being asked. Concise means the response is clear and not verbose or excessive.

Then consider the creativity and novelty of the assistant's answers when needed. Finally, identify any missing important information in the assistants' answers that would be beneficial to include when responding to the user prompt.

After providing your explanation, you must output only one of the following choices as your final verdict with a label:

1. Assistant A is significantly better: [[A>>B]]
2. Assistant A is slightly better: [[A>B]]
3. Tie, relatively the same: [[A=B]]
4. Assistant B is slightly better: [[B>A]]
5. Assistant B is significantly better: [[B>>A]]

Example output: "My final verdict is tie: [[A=B]]".

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 256
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_X, .name="ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_Y, .name="ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_RX, .name="ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_RY, .name="ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TL, .name="L1"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TL2, .name="L2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR, .name="R1"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR2, .name="R2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_NORTH, .name="TRIANGLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SOUTH, .name="CROSS"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_WEST, .name="SQUARE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_EAST, .name="CIRCLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_UP, .name="UP"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name="DOWN"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name="LEFT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name="RIGHT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SELECT, .name="SELECT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_START, .name="START"},
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]); ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(1);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(1);
    }

    while (1) {
        int n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE, 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
        } else {
            int event_index, event_value;
            memcpy(&event_index, buffer, sizeof(int));
            memcpy(&event_value, buffer + sizeof(int), sizeof(int));

            if (event_index >= 0 && event_index < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0])) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].type,
                                            REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].code, event_value);
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
            }
        }
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}

Below are modified versions of the server (in C) and client (in Zig) that now agree on a binary “packet” format consisting of an array of 2‑int16 pairs. In other words, every packet contains one 16‑bit event index followed by a 16‑bit event value for each registered event. (In the example the packet carries 18 pairs.) 

──────────────────────────── Server (C) ────────────────────────────
Below is the updated server code. Note that we now:
1. Include <stdint.h> so that we can use int16_t.
2. Define a struct “event_pair” with two 16‑bit members.
3. Compute the expected number of events (EVENT_COUNT) from REGISTERED_EVENTS.
4. When a UDP packet is received, we verify its length is a multiple of the size of our pair, then iterate over each pair and emit an event using libevdev_uinput_write_event.
5. A single sync (SYN_REPORT) event is sent after processing the entire packet.

-----------------------------------------------------------
/* server.c */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/input.h>  // for EV_* constants

#define BUFFER_SIZE 512  // make sure our buffer is large enough for the entire packet
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_X, .name = "ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_Y, .name = "ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RX, .name = "ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RY, .name = "ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL, .name = "L1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL2, .name = "L2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR, .name = "R1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR2, .name = "R2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_NORTH, .name = "TRIANGLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SOUTH, .name = "CROSS"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_WEST, .name = "SQUARE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_EAST, .name = "CIRCLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_UP, .name = "UP"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name = "DOWN"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name = "LEFT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name = "RIGHT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SELECT, .name = "SELECT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_START, .name = "START"},
};

#define EVENT_COUNT (sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]))

/* Our binary packet format: a sequence of pairs of 16-bit values */
struct event_pair {
    int16_t event_index;
    int16_t event_value;
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < EVENT_COUNT; ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
            continue;
        }

        /* The total number of bytes received should be a multiple of our event_pair size */
        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Received packet with unexpected size: %zd bytes\n", n);
            continue;
        }

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {
            int idx = pairs[i].event_index;
            int val = pairs[i].event_value;
            if (idx >= 0 && idx < EVENT_COUNT) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].type,
                                              REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].code, val);
            }
        }
        /* After all events have been written, send the synchronization event */
        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}
-----------------------------------------------------------

──────────────────────────── Client (Zig) ────────────────────────────
Below is the modified Zig client. The changes are as follows:
1. We now define an EventPair struct (with two i16 fields).
2. Instead of sending a one‐dimensional array of event values, we build an array of EventPair in which each pair consists of the event’s index (the enum’s value) and its current value.
3. Then we send the binary data (the entire array) via UDP.

-----------------------------------------------------------
const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/// Define your controller event indices based on the JSON mapping
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1 = 4,
    L2 = 5,
    R1 = 6,
    R2 = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS = 9,
    SQUARE = 10,
    CIRCLE = 11,
    UP = 12,
    DOWN = 13,
    LEFT = 14,
    RIGHT = 15,
    SELECT = 16,
    START = 17,
};

const EventPair = struct {
    index: i16,
    value: i16,
};

/// Send an entire array of EventPairs to the server.
fn sendControllerState(
    sock: posix.fd_t,
    addr: *const net.Address,
    eventPairs: []const EventPair,
) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(eventPairs);
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len;

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("Sent {d} bytes\n", .{ret});

    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {d} bytes, but sent {d}\n",
            .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

/// Create a UDP socket (for sending only)
fn createUDPSocket() !posix.fd_t {
    return posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
}

/// Initialize controller state; one value per event.
fn initializeControllerState() [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 {
    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(controllerState[0..], 0);
    return controllerState;
}

pub fn main() anyerror!void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;

    // Initialization parameters
    const screenWidth = 800;
    const screenHeight = 450;

    rl.initWindow(screenWidth, screenHeight, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // Initialize controller state (one value per event)
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // Create a UDP socket for sending packets
    const sock = try createUDPSocket();
    defer posix.close(sock);

    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state based on keyboard input.
        // (For this example, we update only the four directional keys.)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Build an array of EventPair where each pair contains the event index and its value.
        const eventCount = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1;
        var eventPairs: [eventCount]EventPair = undefined;
        // Fill in all events – the index is implicit in the array order
        var i: usize = 0;
        while (i < eventCount) : (i += 1) {
            eventPairs[i] = EventPair{
                .index = @intCast(i16, i),
                .value = controllerState[i],
            };
        }

        // Create the destination address; using localhost here.
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, eventPairs[0..]);

        // Draw screen
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.lightGray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}
-----------------------------------------------------------

2. On the Zig side, instead of sending a raw array of values, we build an array of EventPair structs such that each pair explicitly carries its event index and value. This way the information on “which event” and its “state” is self‐contained, matching the “example Zig array” format.

By making these modifications, both the server and the client agree on the same binary format for transmitting the controller state.

const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Event enumeration – mirrors the C side.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1       = 4,
    L2       = 5,
    R1       = 6,
    R2       = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS    = 9,
    SQUARE   = 10,
    CIRCLE   = 11,
    UP       = 12,
    DOWN     = 13,
    LEFT     = 14,
    RIGHT    = 15,
    SELECT   = 16,
    START    = 17,
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Helper: turn a Zig slice of i16 into a byte array.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn asBytes(slice: []const i16) mem.bytes() {
    return std.mem.asBytes(slice);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Send the whole controller state (array of i16) to the UDP socket.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
pub fn sendControllerState(sock: posix.fd_t, addr: *const net.Address, controllerState: []const i16) !void {
    const bytes = asBytes(controllerState);
    const len = bytes.len;                     // number of i16 values = number of bytes to send

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytes, 0, addr.any, addr.getOsSockLen());
    if (ret != len) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {}, but sent {}", .{ len, ret });
    }
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Create a UDP server and bind to 127.0.0.1:31415.
   Returns a tuple (sock, addr).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn createUDPServer() !struct {
    const sock = try posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK.DGRAM, 0);
    const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
    try posix.bind(sock, &addr.any, addr.getOsSockLen());
    return .{ .sock = sock, .addr = addr };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Initialise the whole controller state (all fields zero, then set arrows).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn initializeControllerState() []const i16 []const i16 {
    const N = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START); // 18
    var state: [N]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(state[0..], 0); // clear everything
    // Arrow keys – you can extend this block for other buttons/analogs later
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up))  1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;
    return state;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Main – raylib window + game loop.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
pub fn main() !void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;
    _ = alloc; // we don’t really need a heap allocator here

    const screen_width = 800;
    const screen_height = 450;

    // ----- Raylib setup -------------------------------------------------
    rl.initWindow(screen_width, screen_height, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // ----- Prepare controller state ---------------------------------------
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // ----- UDP socket ----------------------------------------------------
    const sock = try posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK.DGRAM, 0);
    defer posix.close(sock); // close when we exit

    // ----- Main loop ------------------------------------------------------
    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state (arrow keys only – expand as needed)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up))  1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Send the whole array to the server
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, &controllerState);

        // ---- Drawing -------------------------------------------------------
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.light_gray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}

**Key fixes**

* **`sendControllerState`** now sends the *entire* `controllerState` slice (`asBytes(controllerState)`) instead of trying to slice up to `START+1`.  
* No more manual “memcpy” tricks – the whole array is turned into a byte buffer and handed to `posix.sendto`.  
* The client still zero‑initialises the array and sets the arrow‑key flags; you can add more assignments for buttons/analogs later.

### How the binary format now looks

For each event `e` in `REGISTERED_EVENTS` the client stores two `i16`s:

```
byte0 = e.type_index   (0 … 17)
byte1 = e.value        (-32768 … 32767)
```

When the server receives a datagram it reads the first two bytes → `event_index` and `event_value`.  
If `event_index` points to a known entry it writes that event with the supplied value.  
All other bytes in the datagram are ignored – the server simply advances to the next packet.

With this layout the **client** and **server** agree on the exact byte layout, making the communication straightforward and easy to debug.

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
            continue;
        }

        /* The total number of bytes received should be a multiple of our event_pair size */
        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Received packet with unexpected size: %zd bytes\n", n);
            continue;
        }

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {
            int idx = pairs[i].event_index;
            int val = pairs[i].event_value;
            if (idx >= 0 && idx < EVENT_COUNT) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].type,
                                              REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].code, val);
            }
        }
        /* After all events have been written, send the synchronization event */
        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;

    LEFT = 14,
    RIGHT = 15,
    SELECT = 16,
    START = 17,

    value: i16,
};

/// Send an entire array of EventPairs to the server.
fn sendControllerState(
    sock: posix.fd_t,
    addr: *const net.Address,
    eventPairs: []const EventPair,
) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(eventPairs);
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len;

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("Sent {d} bytes\n", .{ret});

    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {d} bytes, but sent {d}\n",
            .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

}

    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 = undefined;

    return controllerState;
}

const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Event enumeration – mirrors the C side.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1       = 4,
    L2       = 5,
    R1       = 6,
    R2       = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS    = 9,
    SQUARE   = 10,
    CIRCLE   = 11,
    UP       = 12,
    DOWN     = 13,
    LEFT     = 14,
    RIGHT    = 15,
    SELECT   = 16,
    START    = 17,
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Helper: turn a Zig slice of i16 into a byte array.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn asBytes(slice: []const i16) mem.bytes() {
    return std.mem.asBytes(slice);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Send the whole controller state (array of i16) to the UDP socket.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
pub fn sendControllerState(sock: posix.fd_t, addr: *const net.Address, controllerState: []const i16) !void {
    const bytes = asBytes(controllerState);
    const len = bytes.len;                     // number of i16 values = number of bytes to send

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytes, 0, addr.any, addr.getOsSockLen());
    if (ret != len) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {}, but sent {}", .{ len, ret });
    }
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Create a UDP server and bind to 127.0.0.1:31415.
   Returns a tuple (sock, addr).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn createUDPServer() !struct {
    const sock = try posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK.DGRAM, 0);
    const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
    try posix.bind(sock, &addr.any, addr.getOsSockLen());
    return .{ .sock = sock, .addr = addr };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Initialise the whole controller state (all fields zero, then set arrows).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
fn initializeControllerState() []const i16 []const i16 {
    const N = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START); // 18
    var state: [N]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(state[0..], 0); // clear everything
    // Arrow keys – you can extend this block for other buttons/analogs later
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up))  1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
    state[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;
    return state;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Main – raylib window + game loop.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
pub fn main() !void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;
    _ = alloc; // we don’t really need a heap allocator here

    const screen_width = 800;
    const screen_height = 450;

    // ----- Raylib setup -------------------------------------------------
    rl.initWindow(screen_width, screen_height, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // ----- Prepare controller state ---------------------------------------
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // ----- UDP socket ----------------------------------------------------
    const sock = try posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK.DGRAM, 0);
    defer posix.close(sock); // close when we exit

    // ----- Main loop ------------------------------------------------------
    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state (arrow keys only – expand as needed)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up))  1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)]  = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Send the whole array to the server
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, &controllerState);

        // ---- Drawing -------------------------------------------------------
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.light_gray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}
```

**Key fixes**

* **`sendControllerState`** now sends the *entire* `controllerState` slice (`asBytes(controllerState)`) instead of trying to slice up to `START+1`.  
* No more manual “memcpy” tricks – the whole array is turned into a byte buffer and handed to `posix.sendto`.  
* The client still zero‑initialises the array and sets the arrow‑key flags; you can add more assignments for buttons/analogs later.

### How the binary format now looks

For each event `e` in `REGISTERED_EVENTS` the client stores two `i16`s:

```
byte0 = e.type_index   (0 … 17)
byte1 = e.value        (-32768 … 32767)
```

When the server receives a datagram it reads the first two bytes → `event_index` and `event_value`.  
If `event_index` points to a known entry it writes that event with the supplied value.  
All other bytes in the datagram are ignored – the server simply advances to the next packet.

With this layout the **client** and **server** agree on the exact byte layout, making the communication straightforward and easy to debug.

fn sendControllerState(sock: posix.fd_t, addr: *const net.Address, controllerState: []const i16) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(controllerState[0..@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START)+1]); // Ensure the entire array is converted to bytes
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len; // Calculate the total number of bytes to send

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("sent {x}\n", .{bytesToSend});
    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {}, but sent {}\n", .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

    const sock = try posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK.DGRAM, 0);

    try posix.bind(sock, &addr.any, addr.getOsSockLen());
    return .{ .sock = sock, .addr = addr };
}

    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START)+1]i16 = undefined;

#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 256
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = { ... };

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = { ... };

    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]); ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(1);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(1);
    }

    while (1) {
        int n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE, 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
        } else {
            int event_index, event_value;
            memcpy(&event_index, buffer, sizeof(int));
            memcpy(&event_value, buffer + sizeof(int), sizeof(int));

            if (event_index >= 0 && event_index < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0])) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].type,
                                            REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].code, event_value);
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
            }
        }
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;

### How the binary format now looks

For each event `e` in `REGISTERED_EVENTS` the client stores two `i16`s:

```
byte0 = e.type_index   (0 … 17)
byte1 = e.value        (-32768 … 32767)
```

When the server receives a datagram it reads the first two bytes → `event_index` and `event_value`.  
If `event_index` points to a known entry it writes that event with the supplied value.  
All other bytes in the datagram are ignored – the server simply advances to the next packet.

With this layout the **client** and **server** agree on the exact byte layout, making the communication straightforward and easy to debug.

#include <string>    // Provides std::string for file paths and values.
#include <thread>    // Provides sleep_for().
#include <chrono>    // Provides seconds for sleep_for().

// Write one value to a sysfs file; return false if the file cannot be opened.
bool writeFile(const std::string& path, const std::string& value) {
    std::ofstream file(path);       // Open the requested sysfs file.
    if (!file) return false;        // Stop if opening the file failed.
    file << value;                  // Write the requested value.
    return static_cast<bool>(file); // Report whether the write succeeded.
}

int main() {
    // Export each GPIO so the kernel creates its gpioN directory.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/export", "17")) return 1; // Motor 1 input A.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/export", "18")) return 1; // Motor 1 input B.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/export", "22")) return 1; // Motor 2 input A.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/export", "23")) return 1; // Motor 2 input B.

    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1)); // Allow GPIO directories to appear.

    // Configure all four GPIO pins as outputs.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/direction", "out")) return 1; // IN1.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/direction", "out")) return 1; // IN2.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/direction", "out")) return 1; // IN3.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/direction", "out")) return 1; // IN4.

    // Run both motors in one direction: each bridge gets one high and one low.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "1")) return 1; // Motor 1 IN1 high.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value", "0")) return 1; // Motor 1 IN2 low.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value", "1")) return 1; // Motor 2 IN3 high.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value", "0")) return 1; // Motor 2 IN4 low.
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(3)); // Let the motors run for 3 seconds.

    // Reverse both motors by swapping the high and low input for each bridge.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "0")) return 1; // Motor 1 IN1 low.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value", "1")) return 1; // Motor 1 IN2 high.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value", "0")) return 1; // Motor 2 IN3 low.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value", "1")) return 1; // Motor 2 IN4 high.
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(3)); // Let them run in reverse.

    // Set both inputs of each bridge low to stop the motors.
    if (!writeFile("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "0")) return 1; // Motor 1 IN1 low.

Ubuntu itself does not provide motor-control GPIO on a typical desktop PC. The example below therefore assumes a Raspberry Pi running Ubuntu, with the Pi’s GPIO connected to an L298N board. It uses **libgpiod v1.x**; GPIO chip names and line offsets can vary by board.

Connect BCM GPIO 17 and 18 to **IN1/IN2**, and GPIO 22 and 23 to **IN3/IN4**. Connect each motor to its corresponding L298N output pair. #include <gpiod.h>   // Provides Linux GPIO control through libgpiod v1.x.
#include <cstdio>    // Provides perror() for reporting system errors.
#include <unistd.h>  // Provides sleep().

int main() {
    gpiod_chip* chip = gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0"); // Open a GPIO chip; its name may differ on your board.
    if (!chip) { perror("gpiod_chip_open"); return 1; }   // Stop if the chip could not be opened.

    gpiod_line* in1 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 17); // Get BCM GPIO 17 for L298N IN1.
    gpiod_line* in2 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 18); // Get BCM GPIO 18 for L298N IN2.
    gpiod_line* in3 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 22); // Get BCM GPIO 22 for L298N IN3.
    gpiod_line* in4 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 23); // Get BCM GPIO 23 for L298N IN4.
    if (!in1 || !in2 || !in3 || !in4) { perror("get GPIO line"); gpiod_chip_close(chip); return 1; } // Check the line lookups.

    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in1, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN1"); return 1; } // Claim IN1 as output, initially low.
    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in2, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN2"); return 1; } // Claim IN2 as output, initially low.
    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in3, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN3"); return 1; } // Claim IN3 as output, initially low.
    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in4, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN4"); return 1; } // Claim IN4 as output, initially low.

    gpiod_line_set_value(in1, 1); // Motor 1 direction: IN1 high.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in2, 0); // Motor 1 direction: IN2 low.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in3, 1); // Motor 2 direction: IN3 high.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in4, 0); // Motor 2 direction: IN4 low.
    sleep(2);                     // Keep both motors in this direction for two seconds.

    gpiod_line_set_value(in1, 0); // Reverse Motor 1 by changing its input state.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in2, 1); // Complete Motor 1's reversed input state.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in3, 0); // Reverse Motor 2 by changing its input state.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in4, 1); // Complete Motor 2's reversed input state.
    sleep(2);                     // Keep both motors in reverse for two seconds.

    gpiod_line_set_value(in1, 0); // Set both inputs low to stop Motor 1 (coast).
    gpiod_line_set_value(in2, 0); // Complete Motor 1's stop state.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in3, 0); // Set both inputs low to stop Motor 2 (coast).
    gpiod_line_set_value(in4, 0); // Complete Motor 2's stop state.

    gpiod_line_release(in2);      // Release the GPIO line for IN2.
    gpiod_line_release(in3);      // Release the GPIO line for IN3.
    gpiod_line_release(in4);      // Release the GPIO line for IN4.
    gpiod_chip_close(chip);       // Close the GPIO chip handle.
    return 0;                     // Exit successfully.

int main() {
    gpiod_chip* chip = gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0"); // Open a GPIO chip; its name may differ on your board.
    if (!chip) { perror("gpiod_chip_open"); return 1; }   // Stop if the chip could not be opened.

    gpiod_line* in1 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 17); // Get BCM GPIO 17 for L298N IN1.
    gpiod_line* in2 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 18); // Get BCM GPIO 18 for L298N IN2.
    gpiod_line* in3 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 22); // Get BCM GPIO 22 for L298N IN3.
    gpiod_line* in4 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, 23); // Get BCM GPIO 23 for L298N IN4.
    if (!in1 || !in2 || !in3 || !in4) { perror("get GPIO line"); gpiod_chip_close(chip); return 1; } // Check the line lookups.

    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in1, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN1"); return 1; } // Claim IN1 as output, initially low.
    if (gpiod_line_request_output(in2, "l298n", 0) < 0) { perror("request IN2"); return 1; } // Claim IN2 as output, initially low.

    gpiod_line_set_value(in3, 0); // Reverse Motor 2 by changing its input state.
    gpiod_line_set_value(in4, 1); // Complete Motor 2's reversed input state.
